title: Release Candidate 1.2.0
description: to close https://github.com/tidymodels/textrecipes/issues/366

title: Add embedding_model2vec() engine for step_sentence_embeddings()
description:
Adds an engine that embeds text with a downloaded Model2Vec model entirely in R, so `step_sentence_embeddings()` can use Model2Vec without Python or a server. Reading the model files still needs the torch and safetensors R packages, and the output hasn't been compared against the Python `model2vec` package.

Closes #301

title: Document training your own embeddings with wordsalad
description:
Adds a "Training your own embeddings" section to the static embeddings vignette, showing how to train vectors with wordsalad's `glove()`, `word2vec()` and `fasttext()` and pass them to `step_word_embeddings()`.

This replaces the dedicated `step_glove()`, `step_fasttext()` and `step_word2vec()` steps proposed in #102, #103 and #104, which I closed as not planned. Training inside `prep()` would be slow, repeat for every resample, and need a large corpus, and `step_word_embeddings()` already accepts any tibble of token vectors. I checked that the output of all three wordsalad functions works with it unchanged.

The section covers matching wordsalad's tokenizer to `step_tokenize()` (its default `space_tokenizer` keeps case and punctuation) and avoiding leakage from assessment data. The chunks stay `eval = FALSE`, so wordsalad is not added to Suggests.

Related to #102, #103, #104.

title: Speed up and reduce memory use of count functions
description:
Makes the feature counting functions used by `step_textfeature()` faster and, for `n_uq_charS`, lighter on memory, without changing any results. This is the pure R route for #267; the remaining `n_uq_charS` allocation is inside stringi, so a C version is still an option if that matters.

Word-list counts are about 2x faster, the `n_uq_*` counts 2 to 5x faster, and peak memory for `n_uq_charS` on 100k documents drops from roughly 450MB to 220MB.

Part of #267.

title: Add step_token_replace()
description:
Adds `step_token_replace()`, which replaces tokens in a token variable using `pattern` and `replacement` vectors, matching exactly by default or with regular expressions. Lemma and part-of-speech attributes are kept since the token count doesn't change.

Closes #134.

title: Add embedding_huggingface() engine for step_sentence_embeddings()
description:
Adds an engine that runs a sentence-transformers model from the Hugging Face Hub through reticulate, so `step_sentence_embeddings()` can use local models without a server. The model is pinned with a required `revision` and only the id and revision are stored in the recipe, never the loaded model. `tidy()` for the step gained a `revision` column to show it.

On macOS, starting Python after recipes is loaded aborts R with an OpenMP error, because data.table and torch each load a `libomp`. The engine sets `KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK` and `OMP_NUM_THREADS` before Python starts when they are unset, and says so, which is the same workaround the text package uses. The cost is a single-threaded model.

## Test plan

Most tests mock the Python boundary. The one live test is skipped unless `sentence_transformers` can be imported. To run it, point reticulate at an environment that has it, for example `RETICULATE_PYTHON=/path/to/venv/bin/python3`, and run `devtools::test(filter = "sentence_embeddings-huggingface")`. It downloads `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` and checks the embeddings against values from sentence-transformers.

Part of #303.

title: Add helpers and a vignette for Model2Vec and BPEmb embeddings
description:
Model2Vec and BPEmb are static embeddings, so they already work with `step_word_embeddings()` once they are in the right table and the text is tokenized to match. This adds helpers to download and read their files into that table, and a vignette with the matching recipes. The vignette code downloads models, so its chunks are not evaluated when it is built.

Part of #303.

title: Add embedding_ollama() engine for step_sentence_embeddings()
description:
Adds `embedding_ollama()`, an engine for `step_sentence_embeddings()` that gets embeddings from a running Ollama server over HTTP, so no Python environment or API key is needed. Also adds a vignette covering how to set up Ollama and what to consider before deploying a recipe that uses it.

Part of #303.

title: Add step_sentence_embeddings()
description:
Adds `step_sentence_embeddings()`, which turns a character column into dense embeddings from a pretrained model, along with `embedding_custom()` for supplying your own embedding function. The step stores a reference to the model rather than the model itself, so recipes stay small and serializable.

Closes #303

title: Add model argument to step_tokenize_sentencepiece()
description:
`step_tokenize_sentencepiece()` can now use a pretrained sentencepiece model, given as a path to a model file, instead of always training one at `prep()` time. The same model is used for all selected columns and is embedded in the prepped step.

Closes #278.

title: Add remove_tags argument to step_pos_filter()
description:
step_pos_filter() could only keep tokens with given part of speech tags. The new `remove_tags` argument does the inverse, dropping the listed tags and keeping everything else. It is mutually exclusive with `keep_tags`.

Closes #218

title: Add vignette giving an overview of the tokenizers
description:
Adds a "Tokenizers" vignette that walks through the tokenization engines and `token` options in the package, showing how each choice and its `options` change the resulting tokens. Examples for engines that need extra setup (tokenizers.bpe, spacyr, udpipe) are shown but not evaluated.

Closes #158

title: Document training_options for the udpipe engine in step_tokenize()
description:
The `training_options` documentation for `step_tokenize()` only mentioned `tokenizers.bpe`, but the `udpipe` engine also requires it to pass the loaded `model`. This documents that and adds an example to the udpipe section.

Closes #237

title: Revise argument documentation to follow the tidyverse style guide
description:
Argument docs across all steps now state defaults, list fixed sets of values, and format code consistently, following the tidyverse style guide. This also corrects the descriptions of `res`, `smooth_idf`, `norm`, and `vocabulary`, and replaces the shared `details-prefix` template with per-step notes on column naming.

Closes #263

title: Link to the functions that do the underlying work in step docs
description:
`step_clean_levels()` and `step_clean_names()` now link to `janitor::make_clean_names()`, the function responsible for the cleaning. A quick sweep found the same gap elsewhere, so the docs for the stemming, stopwords, wordpiece, bpe, LDA and hashing steps now link to the functions they wrap too.

The last commit is the output of `devtools::document()` with roxygen 8.1.0, so it includes some unrelated reformatting.

Closes #198

title: Add vignette on using textrecipes as a sparse matrix engine
description:
Adds a vignette showing how to use textrecipes with recipes alone, without workflows, to get a sparse document-term matrix out of `step_tf()`, `step_tfidf()`, and the hashing steps via `bake(composition = "dgCMatrix")`.

Closes #302

title: Remove thread caps from tests and examples
description:
Closes #252.

Following the approach in posit-dev/skills#80, I measured cpu/elapsed on R-hub `ubuntu-release` (threaded OpenBLAS, about 4 cores) with every thread cap from #251 removed.

* Tests: 1.00 for all 33 test files (24s/24s overall)
* Examples: 57s/56s
* Vignettes: 9s/8s

Nothing is close to the 2.5 threshold, so the `data.table::setDTthreads()`, `OMP_*` and `rsparse` settings are removed from the tests and examples, along with the now unused `data.table` in Suggests. `.claude` is also added to `.Rbuildignore`.

Caveat: this runner has far fewer cores than CRAN's, so it can't prove the NOTE won't return there.

title: Add value-level tests for weighting and feature-extraction steps
description:
Adds tests that check hand-computed expected values, not just shape or dense/sparse identity, for `step_tf()`, `step_tfidf()`, `step_textfeature()`, `step_texthash()` and `step_dummy_hash()`. `step_lda()` and `step_ngram()` already have value checks, so they are untouched.

Closes #328

title: Validate options with check_options() in steps that take options
description:
Uses `recipes::check_options()` in `prep()` for `step_tokenize()`, `step_tokenize_bpe()`, `step_tokenize_sentencepiece()` and `step_stem()`, so non-list, unnamed, or conflicting `options` give a clear error up front instead of failing later or silently misbehaving.

Closes #291

title: Test that all steps support 0 and 1 rows in bake()
description:
Adds a 0 and 1 row `bake()` test to every step, mirroring tidymodels/recipes#1472. The tests turned up bugs with 0 rows in `step_texthash()`, `step_dummy_hash()`, `step_lda()` and `step_pos_filter()`, and zero-length tokenlists losing their lemma and pos fields (which broke `step_lemma()`), all fixed here.

Closes #290

title: Add check_tokenlist() helper for repeated tokenlist input checks
description:
Replaces the repeated `if (!is_tokenlist(x)) abort(...)` blocks in `R/tokenlist.R` with a single `check_tokenlist()` helper, which also unifies the three slightly different error messages.

Closes #272

title: Use recipes_map_cols() in bake() methods that transform columns in place
description:
Converts the 13 `bake()` methods listed in #312 from per-column `new_data[[col]] <- ...` loops to `recipes_map_cols()`, which avoids copying the data frame once per column. Requires recipes >= 1.4.0, the first release exporting it.

Errors raised inside the per-column function now report `fn()` instead of `bake()` as the caller, so three snapshots were updated.

Closes #312

title: Fix step_word_embeddings() docs to match actual behavior
description: Closes #331. The `@details` text described the default `prefix` as `"wordembedding"` and said new column names include the aggregation function name; the actual default is `"wordembed"` and the generated names are `prefix_variable_dimension` (no aggregation function name). Updated the docs and example text to match, and regenerated `man/step_word_embeddings.Rd`.

title: Correct the tf/tfidf denominator in the docs
description: Closes #326. The docs for `step_tf(weight_scheme = "term frequency")` and `step_tfidf(norm = "l1")` said the denominator was the total number of words in the document, but the underlying `rowSums()` is computed on the DTM from `tokenlist_to_dtm()`, which only includes tokens in the trained vocabulary. Any tokens dropped by a custom `vocabulary` or an upstream `step_tokenfilter()` are excluded from both numerator and denominator, so the true denominator is the count of in-vocabulary tokens. Reworded both docs accordingly and regenerated `man/`.

title: Fix crash and errors in step_texthash()/step_dummy_hash()
description:
## Summary

Fixes #314, #289, #304

- **#314**: `step_texthash()` and `step_dummy_hash()` would segfault R (an uncatchable crash) when `num_terms = 0`, because `prep()` allowed `min = 0` through to `text2vec::hash_vectorizer(hash_size = 0)`. Both steps now require `num_terms >= 1`, so this now raises a clean `cli_abort()` during `prep()` instead of crashing.
- **#289**: `step_texthash()` with the default `signed = TRUE` and `sparse = "yes"` could error with `sparsevctrs`' "values value must not be equal to the default 0" when a signed hash collision cancelled out to a true zero. `text2vec::create_dtm()` can leave these as explicit (structural) zero entries in the sparse matrix; `list_to_hash()` now calls `Matrix::drop0()` before coercing to a sparse tibble so these are treated as implicit zeros.
- **#304**: `step_dummy_hash(..., collapse = TRUE, keep_original_cols = TRUE)` failed to restore the original selected columns (it always dropped them when `collapse = TRUE`), and the intermediate collapsed column (e.g. `"artist_title_medium"`) could leak into the baked output. `bake.step_dummy_hash()` now keeps/drops the true original columns via `remove_original_cols()` regardless of `collapse`, and always drops the intermediate collapsed column.

## Test plan

- [x] Added regression tests in `tests/testthat/test-texthash.R` and `tests/testthat/test-dummy_hash.R` for all three issues
- [x] `devtools::test()` run for both affected test files and the full suite: 0 failures, all relevant snapshots updated
- [x] Added a "Bug Fixes" entry to `NEWS.md`

title: Fix dead backwards-compat shim and character-column dictionary in step_clean_levels()
description:
Fixes #321, #320

## Summary

- **#321**: `bake.step_clean_levels()` captured `col_names <- names(object$clean)` *before* the "backwards compatibility with 1.0.3 (#230)" fix-up ran, so for a legacy trained object with no outer names on `object$clean`, `col_names` stayed `NULL`, the fix-up itself was a no-op (`names(object$clean) <- NULL`), and the cleaning loop ran zero times, silently skipping cleaning. Fixed by storing the trained column names in a new dedicated `columns` field on the step (set in `prep()`), mirroring the pattern already used by steps like `step_tokenfilter()`, so `bake()` no longer depends on `names(object$clean)` to know which columns to clean.

- **#320**: `check_type()` allows character (`"string"`) columns, but `prep.step_clean_levels()` built the cleaning dictionary via `levels()`, which is always `NULL` for a character vector. This left the trained dictionary empty for character columns, so `bake()` fell back to calling `janitor::make_clean_names()` directly on the batch of row values, meaning identical inputs could clean differently depending on their position in the batch, and novel values never became `NA`. Fixed by building the dictionary from `unique(as.character(training[[col_name]]))` for non-factor columns (factors still use `levels()`) and applying that fixed, trained lookup at `bake()` time for both factor and character columns.

## Test plan

- [x] Added a repro-based test confirming identical character inputs clean identically regardless of row position, and that novel character values become `NA` at bake time (#320).
- [x] Added a test simulating a legacy trained object with an unnamed `clean` field, confirming `bake()` still cleans data correctly using the new `columns` field (#321).
- [x] Ran `devtools::test(filter = "clean_levels")` (all 24 tests pass, including previously CRAN-skipped snapshot tests).
- [x] Added `NEWS.md` bullets under "Bug fixes" for the development version.

title: Fix non-deterministic and degenerate step_lda() bake output
description:
Fixes #315

## Summary

`bake.step_lda()` (via `word_dims_newtext()`) called `lda_model$fit_transform()` instead of `lda_model$transform()`, so every `bake()` call re-fit topic assignments from whatever documents happened to be present in `new_data`, instead of projecting those documents onto the model already fitted during `prep()`. On top of that, `word_dims_newtext()` rebuilt the vocabulary from `new_data` alone, using different (stricter) pruning than the vocabulary used during `prep()`, so the trained vocabulary/dtm was never actually reused at bake time.

Together these made `step_lda()`'s output both non-deterministic and statistically invalid:

* Baking a single document could give a different, non-zero result depending on what other documents were present in the same `bake()` call, violating the recipes contract that `bake()` is a deterministic, row-independent transform of a fitted step.
* Topic weights frequently didn't sum to ~1 (as they must for an LDA topic distribution), and small batches could come back entirely zero (with a warning that was silently swallowed by `capture.output()`).

### Fix

* `prep.step_lda()` now stores, per selected column, both the fitted LDA model *and* the `text2vec` vectorizer used to build its training dtm.
* `bake.step_lda()` (`word_dims_newtext()`) reuses that same vectorizer to build the new-data dtm (instead of deriving a fresh, differently-pruned vocabulary from `new_data`), and calls `lda_model$transform()` rather than `fit_transform()`.
* Because WarpLDA's `transform()` runs its Gibbs sampler jointly over every document passed to it in one call (and is therefore not row-independent by construction), `word_dims_newtext()` now transforms each document's row of the dtm individually. This guarantees `bake()` output for a given document is identical whether that document is baked alone or as part of a larger batch.
* A backwards-compatibility fallback is kept for recipes that were `prep()`-ed before this fix, which only stored the fitted model (not the vectorizer).
* When a single pre-trained `lda_models` object is supplied and reused across multiple selected columns, each column now gets its own cloned/fitted copy, since the previous prep-time fitting could otherwise leave the shared object holding only the last column's vocabulary.

This is a correctness-critical fix: `step_lda()`'s topic features were previously non-deterministic and, in many cases, degenerate (didn't sum to 1, or were entirely zero for small batches).

## Test plan

- [x] Added tests in `tests/testthat/test-lda.R` asserting:
  - baking a single document alone gives identical output to baking that same document as part of a 100-row batch
  - topic weight rows sum to ~1 (within floating point tolerance) for documents with at least one token surviving vocabulary pruning
  - baking a small 5-row batch works without warnings and returns non-zero topic weights
- [x] Updated `tests/testthat/_snaps/lda.md` snapshot: a spurious `dtm has 0 rows. Empty iterator?` warning that used to fire during `prep()` (via the internal bake-to-update-training-data step, using the old broken vocabulary) no longer occurs.
- [x] Confirmed the existing `step_lda()` roxygen examples (default model, custom `num_topics`, and a shared pre-trained model reused across two columns) all run successfully.
- [x] `devtools::test()` passes: 609 passing, 0 failing, 38 skipped (optional deps not installed).

title: Fix tokenizer dispatch bugs in tokenizer_fun and engine closures
description:
Fixes #319, #318, #248

## Summary

All three issues live in the shared tokenizer dispatch mechanism (`tokenizer_fun()` in `R/tokenize.R` and the per-engine closures it calls).

- **#248**: `tokenizer_fun()` built the call as `token(x = x)`, so a `custom_token` function whose first parameter isn't literally named `x` failed with "unused argument". It now builds the call positionally (`token(x)`), so any parameter name works.
- **#318**: `tokenizer_fun()` assigned the tokenizer's output straight into `new_data[[col_name]]` with no length check. If a tokenizer returned a list shorter than the input, R silently recycled it, duplicating rows with no warning. `tokenizer_fun()` now checks `length(out) == length(x)` and raises a `cli_abort()` naming the offending column when they don't match.
- **#319**: The bake-time closures for `engine = "spacyr"` (`R/tokenizer-spacyr.R`), `engine = "tokenizers.bpe"` (`R/tokenizer-tokenizersbpe.R`), and `sentencepiece` (`R/tokenizer-sentencepiece.R`) only accepted `x`, with no `...`, unlike the existing `udpipe`/`wordpiece` closures. Since `tokenizer_fun()` re-passes the step's `options` at bake time via `rlang::call_modify()`, any non-empty `options` crashed with "unused argument". These closures now accept `...` (matching the `udpipe`/`wordpiece` pattern):
  - `spacyr`: `...` is forwarded into `spacyr::spacy_parse()`, since spacyr has no separate training step and its options genuinely apply at each tokenization call.
  - `tokenizers.bpe` / `sentencepiece`: `...` is accepted but intentionally *not* forwarded into `bpe_encode()`/`sentencepiece_encode()`, since those `options` only make sense for training the model (`bpe()`/`sentencepiece()`) and have no meaning for encoding already-trained models. Docs for `options` on `step_tokenize()`, `step_tokenize_bpe()`, and `step_tokenize_sentencepiece()` were updated to clarify this train-vs-bake distinction.

## Testing

- Added tests in `tests/testthat/test-tokenize.R` for a `custom_token` function whose argument isn't named `x` (#248) and for a `custom_token` function that returns a too-short list, verifying the new `cli_abort()` (#318).
- Added tests in `tests/testthat/test-tokenize_bpe.R` and `tests/testthat/test-tokenize_sentencepiece.R` (guarded with `skip_if_not_installed()`, since those packages aren't installed in this environment) verifying `bake()` no longer errors when training-only `options` are set (#319).
- Added a similar `spacyr`-guarded test in `test-tokenize.R`.
- Full test suite: `devtools::test()` → 605 pass, 0 fail (41 skipped for optional packages not installed locally: spacyr, tokenizers.bpe, sentencepiece, wordpiece).

## Test plan

- [x] `devtools::test()` passes locally with 0 failures
- [x] New tests reproduce and verify fixes for #248 and #318 without needing optional packages
- [x] New tests for #319 guarded with `skip_if_not_installed()` for spacyr/tokenizers.bpe/sentencepiece
- [x] NEWS.md updated with bug fix bullets referencing #319, #318, #248

title: Fix step_tokenmerge() reading nonexistent object$column field
description:
Fixes #332

`bake.step_tokenmerge()` read `object$column`, which only "worked" because R's `$` partial-matches it against the actual field `object$columns`. Changed to `object$columns` so the code doesn't rely on fragile partial matching.

title: Preserve lemma/pos attributes through step_stem()
description:
Fixes #327

## Summary
`tokenlist_apply()` (used by `bake.step_stem()`) rebuilt the stemmed tokenlist with only the `tokens` field, silently dropping any `lemma`/`pos` attributes set by an earlier POS-tagging tokenization step (e.g. via the spacyr or udpipe tokenizer engines). This caused `step_pos_filter()`/`step_lemma()` applied after `step_stem()` to fail with a misleading error ("doesn't have a pos attribute... make sure the tokenization step includes part of speech tagging") even though POS tagging had in fact been done upstream, because `step_stem()` had already dropped it.

Since stemming is applied element-wise per token and does not change token count or ordering, `lemma`/`pos` stay aligned with the stemmed tokens and can simply be carried through unchanged, the same way `tokenlist_filter_function()` already forwards these attributes.

## Changes
- `tokenlist_apply()` in `R/tokenlist.R` now forwards `lemma`/`pos` from the input tokenlist into the reconstructed output tokenlist.
- Updated `tokenlist_apply` unit tests in `tests/testthat/test-tokenlist.R` to assert `lemma`/`pos` are preserved.
- Added a `step_stem()` integration test in `tests/testthat/test-stem.R` reproducing the issue: builds a synthetic tokenlist with `lemma`/`pos` set (no spacyr/udpipe dependency needed), stems it, and confirms the attributes survive unchanged.
- Added a NEWS.md bullet under Bug fixes.

## Test plan
- [x] `testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-tokenlist.R")` passes
- [x] `testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-stem.R")` passes
- [x] Manually reproduced the original issue's `step_stem() |> step_pos_filter()` pipeline end-to-end and confirmed it now bakes successfully instead of erroring

title: Fix count_functions.R word-list and doc/impl bugs
description:
Fixes #316, #329

## Summary

**#316**: `first_person()`, `first_personp()`, `second_person()`, `second_personp()`, `third_person()`, `to_be()`, and `prepositions()` (all used by `step_textfeature()`) tested `word_list %in% whole_document_string`, i.e. whether a listed word was literally equal to the *entire* document, rather than whether the document contained that word as a token. As a result they almost always returned 0:

```r
to_be(c("This is a test string", "we are the champions"))
#> [1] 0 0   # both clearly contain "is"/"are"
```

Fixed by tokenizing each document into lower-cased words with `stringi::stri_extract_all_words()` before testing membership against the (already lower-case) word lists.

**#329**: three additional doc/implementation mismatches in the same file:

- `n_uq_urls()` extracted only the literal substring `"http"`/`"https"`, so distinct url counts were capped at 2 regardless of how many distinct urls were actually present. Now extracts the full url (`"https?://\S+"`) before counting distinct matches.
- `n_charS()`/`n_uq_charS()` documented excluding urls, hashtags, and mentions from the character count but only ever stripped whitespace. They now actually strip urls, hashtags, and mentions (reusing the same regexes as the dedicated counting functions) before counting.
- `n_extraspaces()` used `"\s{2}|\t|\n"`, which also fired on a single tab or newline, contradicting the "more than 1 consecutive space" documentation. Simplified to `"\s{2,}"`, which only matches runs of 2+ whitespace characters (tabs/newlines still count when repeated).
- NA handling was inconsistent across the file: `n_*` functions mostly returned `NA`, `n_uq_*` returned `1`, and the person/preposition functions returned `0`. All counting functions now consistently return `NA` for `NA` input.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `tests/testthat/test-count_functions.R` with value-based assertions (not just shape/type) for all 7 fixed person/preposition functions, `n_uq_urls()` with multiple distinct urls, `n_charS()`/`n_uq_charS()` with urls/hashtags/mentions present, `n_extraspaces()` distinguishing a single tab/newline from 2+ consecutive whitespace, and NA propagation across every function in `count_functions`.
- [x] `devtools::test()` passes with 0 failures (673 pass, 38 skip for optional deps not installed locally).
- [x] Added NEWS.md bullets under Bug fixes referencing #316 and #329.

title: Fix show_tokens() n argument max bound validation
description:
Fixes #322

## Summary

- `R/show_tokens.R` called `check_number_whole(n, min = 0, nrow(rec$template))`. Since `check_number_whole()`'s `max` argument is name-only (after `...`), the positional `nrow(rec$template)` landed in `...` instead of being bound to `max`, so the upper bound was never actually validated. Worse, whenever validation needed to fail for another reason, the stray `...` argument corrupted the error-reporting call and produced a nonsensical error like `` `class` must be a character vector, not the number 2. `` instead of a useful message about `n`.
- Fixed by explicitly naming the argument: `check_number_whole(n, min = 0, max = as.double(nrow(rec$template)))` (`max` also requires a double, so `nrow()`'s integer result is coerced).
- Two roxygen examples (`R/show_tokens.R` and `R/tokenize.R`) relied on the default `n = 6L` exceeding the number of rows in their 2-row example tibble, which is now correctly rejected instead of silently truncated. Updated those examples to pass `n = 2` explicitly. Corresponding `.Rd` files were hand-edited to match (the repo's pinned `RoxygenNote` doesn't match the roxygen2 version available locally, so `devtools::document()` wasn't run to avoid unrelated regeneration noise).

## Tests

- Added `tests/testthat/test-show_tokens.R` (previously no test file existed for `show_tokens()`), covering: happy-path usage on a prepped tokenize recipe, respecting `n`, and clear errors (verified via snapshot) when `n` exceeds the upper bound, falls below the lower bound, or isn't a whole number.
- `devtools::test(filter = "show_tokens")` passes (10/10), and the full test suite passes with only pre-existing skips for unavailable optional NLP engines (spacyr, tokenizers.bpe, sentencepiece, wordpiece).

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced the original bug: `show_tokens()` with `n` above `nrow(rec$template)` did not error, and `n` values that trigger other validation failures (e.g. non-whole numbers) produced the nonsensical `class` error.
- [x] Confirmed the fix produces clear, accurate error messages referencing `n` and its bounds.
- [x] Added and ran new tests; full suite passes.

title: Fix ngram argument validation and non-UTF-8 encoding bugs
description:
Fixes #324, #323

## Summary

**#324 — argument validation:**
- `check_number_whole()` in `prep.step_ngram()` and `prep.step_sequence_onehot()` used `min = 0` even though the documented minimum for `num_tokens`, `min_num_tokens`, and `sequence_length` is 1. Changed to `min = 1` so invalid values (0, negative) fail with a clear message at the R level instead of falling through to unrelated low-level errors (a cryptic C error for ngram, a `dimnames` mismatch caused by a `paste()` zero-length-argument quirk for sequence_onehot).
- Added an explicit `min_num_tokens <= num_tokens` check in `prep.step_ngram()` using `cli_abort()`, so this case now surfaces a clear, on-topic error instead of relying on the C-level check.
- Fixed a typo in the C-level error message: "n_min must be less then n." -> "n_min must be less than n."

**#323 — non-UTF-8 encoding bug:**
- `fill_one_ngram()` in `src/ngram.c` read input strings with `CHAR(STRING_ELT(x, i))` (raw bytes) but always tagged the output as `CE_UTF8` via `Rf_mkCharCE()`, without ever calling `Rf_translateCharUTF8()`. For latin1/native-encoded input (common on Windows or with legacy-encoded text), this produced strings mislabeled as UTF-8 whose bytes were not valid UTF-8, causing real errors in downstream operations like `nchar()` and `toupper()`, not just a cosmetic display issue.
- Fixed by reading input bytes with `Rf_translateCharUTF8()` in both the size-computation pass and the fill pass, so the subsequent `CE_UTF8` tagging is now correct.

## Test plan

- [x] Added tests in `tests/testthat/test-ngram.R` and `tests/testthat/test-sequence_onehot.R` covering `num_tokens`/`min_num_tokens`/`sequence_length` = 0, and `min_num_tokens > num_tokens`, with updated snapshots.
- [x] Added a test exercising the encoding fix (constructs latin1 bytes via `iconv()`, skips gracefully if that's not reliable on the test platform, and checks `Encoding()`, `nchar()`, and `toupper()` on the ngram output).
- [x] `devtools::load_all()` (recompiles the C code) then `devtools::test(filter = "ngram")`, `devtools::test(filter = "sequence_onehot")`, and `devtools::test(filter = "tokenlist")` all pass locally.
- [x] NEWS.md updated with bug fix bullets referencing #324 and #323.

title: Fix negative TF-IDF values when sublinear_tf = TRUE
description:
Fixes #317

## Summary

- `dtm_to_tfidf()` in `R/tfidf.R` normalized the raw term-count matrix *before* applying the `sublinear_tf` transform (`1 + log(TF)`). By the time the log was taken, `dtm@x` held row-normalized fractions (typically < 1), so `log()` could return a large negative number and `1 + log(fraction)` could go negative, producing negative TF-IDF scores after multiplying by a non-negative IDF weight.
- The fix swaps the order: apply the sublinear transform to the raw counts first, then normalize. This matches the documented behavior ("replace the term frequency with 1 + log(TF)") and keeps values non-negative for TF >= 1. IDF weights are computed separately at `prep()` time from the raw document-term matrix and are unaffected by this ordering change.
- Added a regression test in `tests/testthat/test-tfidf.R` that hand-computes the expected TF-IDF value for the repro case from the issue (doc with 7 occurrences of "a", 1 of "b"), asserts the actual output matches within tolerance, and asserts non-negativity across `norm = "l1"/"l2"/"none"` on a more realistic corpus. Previously the only `sublinear_tf` tests checked dense/sparse output identity, which passed even with the bug since both paths used the same (buggy) code.
- Added a NEWS.md bullet under a new "Bug fixes" section for the development version.

## Test plan

- [x] Reproduced the bug from the issue (negative TF-IDF values)
- [x] Applied the fix and confirmed the repro now produces the hand-computed non-negative values
- [x] `devtools::test(filter = "tfidf")` passes: 49 passed, 0 failed (including existing dense == sparse identity tests)

title: Speed up step_word_embeddings()
description:
> [!NOTE]
> This PR is a showcase of using [{debrief}](https://github.com/jcheng5/debrief) to drive a profiling-based optimization. Each iteration below came from profiling with `profvis` + `debrief`.
## Origin

This started from the following prompt:

> look the following code
>
> ```r
> library(recipes)
> library(textrecipes)
>
> embeddings <- tibble(
>   tokens = c("the", "cat", "ran"),
>   d1 = c(1, 0, 0),
>   d2 = c(0, 1, 0),
>   d3 = c(0, 0, 1)
> )
>
> sample_data <- tibble(
>   text = c(
>     "The.",
>     "The cat.",
>     "The cat ran."
>   ),
>   text_label = c("fragment", "fragment", "sentence")
> )
>
> rec <- recipe(text_label ~ ., data = sample_data) |>
>   step_tokenize(text) |>
>   step_word_embeddings(text, embeddings = embeddings)
>
> rec |> prep() |> bake(sample_data)
> ```
>
> I want to See if there are room for improvements. specifically in the step_word_embeddings part.
>
> Use the debrief package like so:
>
> ```r
> library(profvis)
> library(debrief)
>
> # Profile some code
> p <- profvis({
>   # your code here
> })
>
> # Get help on available functions
> pv_help()
>
> # Start with a summary
> pv_print_debrief(p)
> ```
>
> you will need to profile this line
>
> ```r
> rec |> prep() |> bake(sample_data)
> ```
>
> This is a iterative process. In a document write down each itteration that you take. Do a commit for each accepted change. you might need to generate new data for embeddings and sample_data to properly test the speed as this data set is quite small

## Summary

Speeds up the `bake()` path of `step_word_embeddings()`, which was driven by `tokenlist_embedding()` in `R/tokenlist.R`. The original implementation sliced the embedding tibble by row and ran a dplyr `group_by()` + `summarise_all()` pipeline per document. This was rewritten over several profiling-driven iterations into matrix/sparse-matrix operations.

On a benchmark of 5,000 documents (10-30 tokens each), a 50,000-token vocabulary, and 100 embedding dimensions:

| aggregation | baseline | this PR | speedup |
|-------------|----------|---------|---------|
| sum         | 0.85 s   | 0.027 s | ~31x |
| mean        | 0.85 s   | 0.027 s | ~31x |
| min         | 0.85 s   | 0.325 s | ~2.6x |
| max         | 0.85 s   | 0.301 s | ~2.8x |

Output is identical to before for all four aggregations, including documents with no matched tokens falling back to `aggregation_default`. All `word_embeddings` tests pass.

## Iterations

The work was done as a sequence of profile-measure-change steps (full notes and benchmark script live in `bench/`, which is `.Rbuildignore`d).

**Baseline.** Profiling showed nearly all the cost in `tokenlist_embedding()`: slicing a 100-column **tibble** by row (`vec_slice`, ~140 MB allocated) and the dplyr group/summarise machinery, plus heavy GC.

**Iteration 1: matrix + `rowsum`.** Convert the embeddings to a numeric matrix and slice rows from it (matrix slicing is far cheaper than tibble slicing), pass the aggregation name through instead of an opaque closure, and aggregate `sum`/`mean` with base `rowsum()`. → sum/mean ~13x; min/max ~2.2x (still using a per-group `apply()`).

**Iteration 2: vectorise min/max.** Replace the per-group `apply()` with a loop over the ~100 embedding columns, each aggregated by a single `tapply()` (far fewer iterations). → modest further gain on min/max.

**Iteration 3: sparse incidence product for sum/mean.** Re-profiling showed `rowsum.default` and the row-slice as the new hot spots. Replaced them with a single sparse-by-dense matrix product: a (n_doc x n_vocab) document-token incidence matrix times the dense embedding matrix yields per-document sums directly, in document order, with no row-slice and no grouped reduction. The **embedding matrix stays dense** here; only the incidence matrix is sparse, and it is sparse by construction (each document holds only a few of the vocabulary's tokens) regardless of the embedding values. `Matrix` is already a dependency. → sum/mean ~19-22x.

**Iteration 4: precompute the dense matrix in `prep()`.** `as.matrix()` was running on every `bake()`, allocating the whole ~40 MB embedding matrix each call and driving much of the GC. Moved the conversion into `prep()`: the prepped step now stores a dense `emb_matrix` plus an `emb_tokens` lookup vector instead of the embeddings tibble (no memory duplication, since an all-numeric matrix is no larger than the tibble), and `tidy()` reads the row count from `emb_matrix`. → sum/mean roughly halved again, ~31x overall.

### Rejected experiments

For min/max I also tried a single flattened `tapply` over all columns at once (~2x *slower*) and an `order()` + `duplicated(fromLast=)` pick per column (~12% faster). The latter's gain was too small for the added complexity on a non-default path, so it was not kept.

## Notes

- The default `sum`/`mean` path is now down to tokenization plus the intrinsic matrix multiply; there is little structural overhead left to remove.
- The full `devtools::test()` run segfaults inside an unrelated `ngram` C-code test under `load_all`; this reproduces on a clean `main` tree (pre-existing, not caused by this PR). The `word_embeddings` tests pass (40 PASS).

title: Add R4.6 snapshot variants for BPE tests
description:
## Problem

The GHA checks on #309 (and any current PR) fail on Windows R CMD check with two test failures, unrelated to that PR's `step_word_embeddings()` work:

```
── Failure ('test-tokenize_bpe.R:169:3'): Errors if vocabulary size is set to low. ──
Adding new snapshot for variant 'R4.6'
── Failure ('test-tokenizer-tokenizersbpe.R:198:3'): Errors if vocabulary size is set to low. ──
Adding new snapshot for variant 'R4.6'
```

## Cause

Both tests use `expect_snapshot(variant = r_version())`, where `r_version()` is `paste0("R", getRversion()[, 1:2])`. The CI runners were bumped to **R 4.6.0**, so `r_version()` now returns `"R4.6"`. There were variant snapshot directories for `R4.3`, `R4.4`, and `R4.5` but none for `R4.6`, so testthat treats it as a brand-new snapshot, which is a failure under CI.

## Fix

The expected error messages here are generated by textrecipes itself and are byte-identical across R 4.3-4.5, so this adds an `R4.6` variant directory copied from the existing `R4.5` snapshots.

(The macOS R-CMD-check failure on #309 is separate: `recipes` failed to `dyn.load` on the R 4.6.0 arm64 runner, a transient upstream binary issue not addressed here.)

title: Avoid nested `unwind_protect()` and unsafe `string` usage
description:
We have taken a long hard look at manual usage of `unwind_protect()` in cpp11 and determined that it is unsafe to use it in a "nested" way. Indeed, if you were to put an `Rf_error()` call (imitating an R error) inside the `unwind_protect()` call of `fill_one_ngram()`, then it causes R to crash. So once thing this PR does is remove the outer `unwind_protect()` call, which wasn't actually impacting performance much.

In https://github.com/r-lib/cpp11/pull/327 we have some new FAQ recommendations that advise against calling `unwind_protect()` yourself _at all_ if possible, with the one exception of character vector manipulation, as we have here.

It is fairly hard to call `unwind_protect()` yourself in a safe way, you have to be careful not to violate these rules:
- You can't use the cpp11 API inside it
- You can't throw exceptions
- You can't create objects that have destructors

We actually violated 2 of these here.
- `std::string` objects were being created inside the `unwind_protect()` and those have destructors. If an R error was thrown from inside the unwind-protect, then that destructor would not be run and you'd get a memory leak. I've worked around this by moving the `std::string` declaration out of the unwind-protect, which should allow its destructor to always run.
- Secondly, `std::string` methods like the `+` method can throw exceptions in rare cases. One way to avoid this is to use pure C here instead, but that is somewhat difficult, so instead I wrapped the places where exceptions were possible in a try/catch, which avoids throwing the exception across a C stack frame (which is undefined behavior). I tried manually adding in `throw std::runtime_error("oh no")` and it does indeed catch the exception safely.

I am sending in a new update of cpp11 in soon. I don't think it actually breaks textrecipes, but you should probably try to get this release in sooner rather than later just to be on the safe side (since these problems are present regardless of the version of cpp11 you have)

title: Spacy extension
description:
This PR adds 

- a `spacyr` engine to `step_tokenize()`
- a `step_lemma()` function to extract lemmatization from tokenlists
- a `step_pos_filter()` function to filter a tokenlist based on part of speech tags

``` r
library(textrecipes)
dat <- tibble(text = c("hello there", "lovely ladies"))


recipe(~ text, data = dat) %>%
  step_tokenize(all_predictors(), engine = "spacyr") %>%
  step_tf(all_predictors()) %>%
  prep() %>%
  juice()
#> # A tibble: 2 x 4
#>   tf_text_hello tf_text_ladies tf_text_lovely tf_text_there
#>           <dbl>          <dbl>          <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1             1              0              0             1
#> 2             0              1              1             0

recipe(~ text, data = dat) %>%
  step_tokenize(all_predictors(), engine = "spacyr") %>%
  step_lemma(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_tf(all_predictors()) %>%
  prep() %>%
  juice()
#> # A tibble: 2 x 4
#>   tf_text_hello tf_text_lady tf_text_lovely tf_text_there
#>           <dbl>        <dbl>          <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1             1            0              0             1
#> 2             0            1              1             0

recipe(~ text, data = dat) %>%
  step_tokenize(all_predictors(), engine = "spacyr") %>%
  step_pos_filter(all_predictors(), keep_tags = "NOUN") %>%
  step_tf(all_predictors()) %>%
  prep() %>%
  juice()
#> # A tibble: 2 x 1
#>   tf_text_ladies
#>            <dbl>
#> 1              0
#> 2              1
```

title: move tuneable.step_ngram to tune package
description:
This PR will together with https://github.com/tidymodels/dials/pull/135 and https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/pull/257 be able to close #94.

``` r
library(tidymodels)
#> ── Attaching packages ────────────────────────────────────────── tidymodels 0.1.1 ──
#> ✓ broom     0.7.0           ✓ recipes   0.1.13.9000
#> ✓ dials     0.0.8.9000      ✓ rsample   0.0.7      
#> ✓ dplyr     1.0.0           ✓ tibble    3.0.3      
#> ✓ ggplot2   3.3.2           ✓ tidyr     1.1.0      
#> ✓ infer     0.5.3           ✓ tune      0.1.1.9000 
#> ✓ modeldata 0.0.2           ✓ workflows 0.1.2      
#> ✓ parsnip   0.1.2           ✓ yardstick 0.0.7      
#> ✓ purrr     0.3.4
#> ── Conflicts ───────────────────────────────────────────── tidymodels_conflicts() ──
#> x purrr::discard() masks scales::discard()
#> x dplyr::filter()  masks stats::filter()
#> x dplyr::lag()     masks stats::lag()
#> x recipes::step()  masks stats::step()
library(textrecipes)

data("okc_text")

okc_long <- okc_text %>%
  pivot_longer(everything())

rec_spec <- recipe(name ~ value, data = okc_long) %>%
  step_tokenize(value) %>%
  step_ngram(value, num_tokens = tune(), min_num_tokens = 1) %>%
  step_tokenfilter(value) %>%
  step_tfidf(value)

mod_spec <- null_model() %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("parsnip")

param_grid <- grid_regular(num_tokens())

okc_folds <- vfold_cv(okc_long, strata = name, v = 2)

wf_spec <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(rec_spec) %>%
  add_model(mod_spec)


lasso_rs <- tune_grid(
  wf_spec,
  resamples = okc_folds,
  grid = param_grid, 
  control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)
)
#> i Fold1: recipe 1/3
#> ✓ Fold1: recipe 1/3
#> i Fold1: recipe 1/3, model 1/1

title: Steps to clean names and factor levels

Closes #100.

This is WIP for now as I get the other step ready.

The new `step_clean_levels()` finds the levels of the nominal variable(s), cleans them, and then uses the new levels to recode:

smith_te <- Smithsonian[16:20,]
